hook: The chip inside your phone started as ordinary sand.

blocks.narration: The chip inside your phone started as ordinary sand. Turning it into billions of transistors is one of humanity's hardest feats.
blocks.visual: Photoreal macro shot of golden sand grains morphing into a shining silicon wafer, clean light

blocks.narration: First, silicon is extracted and purified to extreme levels, often around ninety-nine point nine nine nine nine nine nine nine percent pure.
blocks.visual: Glowing molten silicon pours in a pristine industrial furnace

blocks.narration: A seed crystal is slowly pulled from the molten silicon, growing one huge single crystal, called an ingot, as it slowly rotates.
blocks.visual: A shimmering cylindrical ingot rises slowly out of a glowing crucible

blocks.narration: The ingot is sliced into ultra-thin discs called wafers, then polished until they are smoother than almost anything else on Earth.
blocks.visual: A diamond saw slices the ingot into mirror-like wafers that catch rainbow reflections

blocks.narration: Next comes photolithography. Light shines through a pattern onto the wafer, printing circuit designs far smaller than a virus.
blocks.visual: Beams of violet light project intricate circuit patterns onto a spinning wafer

blocks.narration: The most advanced machines use extreme ultraviolet light, made by blasting tiny tin droplets with powerful lasers, tens of thousands of times per second.
blocks.visual: Inside a futuristic machine, laser pulses strike tiny falling droplets, bursting into violet light

blocks.narration: These machines are made by one company, ASML, and each costs well over a hundred million dollars. Every layer gets etched and repeated.
blocks.visual: A gigantic machine the size of a bus sits in a clean room, workers in white suits around it

blocks.narration: Finally the wafer is cut into individual chips and tested. Comment which piece of tech we should break down next.
blocks.visual: A finished wafer splits into hundreds of tiny glinting chips, camera pulls back

cta: Comment which piece of tech we should break down next.

captions.hook_line: Your phone's chip started as sand. Here's how it becomes billions of transistors 💻
captions.body: Chipmakers purify silicon to extreme levels, grow single-crystal ingots, slice them into wafers and pattern them with light. The most advanced chips use extreme ultraviolet lithography at a 13.5 nanometer wavelength, made by machines from ASML that cost well over $100 million each.

youtube_title: How Computer Chips Are Made From Sand
